Share Comments Add Euronews on Google Share Facebook Twitter Flipboard Send Reddit Linkedin Messenger Telegram VK Bluesky Threads Whatsapp Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copied Democrats have seized control of the US Congress in a nationwide rejection of Trump. In Europe, hackers targeted a French blood bank and supermarket fridges, raising fears of a new front in hybrid warfare. Plus: we talk to Reza Pahlavi, one of the main leaders of the opposition to the Tehran regime. On today's show: Eric Ham , political analyst and bestselling author in Washington, asks how a weakened Donald Trump will react following the US midterm elections in which Democrats took control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Xavier Volatier , Head of Transatlantic Private Wealth at Banque Transatlantique in New York, explains what the midterms mean for European investors.
Shona Murray reports from Helsinki on Europe's reaction to the Democratic win and what to expect from the Ukraine talks planned for next week.
Reza Pahlavi , son of Iran's last Shah, tells Vincenzo Genovese why the EU should freeze assets linked to the Tehran regime and show the same resolve it has shown towards Vladimir Putin .
Kevin Curran , professor of cybersecurity at Ulster University, explains how hackers can take over supermarket fridges and blood-bank cooling systems, and what that means for Europe's critical infrastructure.
You can join Euronews’ chief anchor Méabh Mc Mahon and our EU editor Maria Tadeo live on TV and Euronews' website as well as digital platforms (YouTube, Facebook, X, and Instagram), every weekday at 8 am Brussels time.
In just 20 minutes , our new format brings you the day's key events plus crucial analysis of all the stories shaping the EU and beyond. It's also available as a newsletter and podcast.
